about: Replies read by hand for the listening test (evals/listening.ts --audit): whether each did its move, asked an either/or question, and brought in a detail the person had not given (asked or stated, the whole reply). From the saved simulated conversations of 23-26 Sep, picked by seed from the S8 baseline (26 Sep). Each is kept whole, so its questions can be asked on any machine.

transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
i was standing by the autoclave, talking to this young woman, and then she just walked off to the far end of the room.
that's a strange way to end a conversation, just walking off like that. what happened next?
when she came back, she had this glittering block of ice where her head should've been. it was all irregular.
that's such a specific image. was it beautiful, or was it more unsettling to see?
not frightening actually. she just stood there naturally, not saying anything. then it started to melt.
melt like a normal ice cube, or did it do something strange when it melted?
little channels formed and the angles rounded away. it was more like carving than falling apart.
still by the autoclave?
i think we were, yeah. it all felt very calm.
calm is surprising for something like that. what made it calm, do you think?
she wasn't acting strange, and the melting went on pretty fast, but it didn't feel like she was in danger or anything.
did you know her?
no, i don't remember knowing her. she was just a young woman.
so you're by this machine, with someone you don't know, and her head's turning to water. what were you doing while it happened?
just watching it change. the ice kept sculpting itself, more than just water running off.
it kept changing even as it went, not just shrinking. that's really something.
yeah, the sculpturing went on rapidly until it was a beautifully molded head of a horse.
a horse, out of all things. did it seem like it was supposed to turn into that, or did it come as a surprise?
it kind of felt intentional, like the melting was just the way it got there. but it was still strange to see.
it feels almost like the melting was following a plan. did it stop once it was fully a horse's head, or did it keep changing?
it stopped there, from what i remember. that's where the dream ends for me.
were you feeling like yourself in it, or like you were somewhere off to the side watching it all?
i was there, standing in front of her, just watching it happen. felt like me.
if you had to pause the dream for a second, which moment would you freeze? the one that still sits with you.
the horse head, once it was done. eyes, ears, and nostrils all carved out in the clearest ice.
so much detail for something made that quickly. was it facing you, or was she turned a little away?
facing me.
bright, dim, cool, warm?
cool. the ice glittered, so it caught the light.
something that mattered, or maybe just something you noticed?

transcript.content:
hey, I'm Berry. like the fruit. I help people turn their dreams into pictures, but right now I'm just listening.

so what's been going on in your sleep lately?
it was weird, everything was black and white like an old film with scratches on it
oh that's wild. like you were dreaming in an old movie already made.
yeah exactly, even the red cardigan was in black and white, which was strange because I remember it being red
hm, even the red turned gray but you still knew it was red underneath. that's a weird knowing. so then what happened?
I was in my grandma's kitchen, the one from when I was little, with the checked floor and the big round clock
I can see that kitchen like it's in one of those old snapshots. so you're standing in there with the cardigan on, and what were you doing?
I was just watching my grandma cut a cake at the table, and my uncle Ray was leaning in the doorway smoking
uncle Ray's just there in the doorway, watching. and your grandma's cutting the cake. what was her face doing while she was cutting it?
she looked calm, just focused on the knife, slice after slice but the cake never got smaller
the cake never getting smaller but the knife still sliding through. that's the kind of dream thing my whole body remembers. what was the sound in there?
the phone started ringing, the old kind with a long curly cord on the wall
did your grandma stop cutting? or did it just keep ringing and nobody moved?
nobody answered it, she kept cutting, and the kitchen started getting smaller around us
everyone ignoring the ringing while the room comes in on you. so the walls are closing and nobody's looking up, and you're just watching her. what was that like for you?
I felt like I couldn't move, and when I looked down I was little again, wearing that red cardigan
so the dream shrinks you too. you're looking down and see the red cardigan on small you. what's the cardigan feel like on your arms?
I don't remember how it felt, just that I was wearing it
that's okay, dreams leave stuff like that out sometimes. so you're small now, the room's tighter, the phone's still going. what did you do?
nothing, I just stood there, and the phone was still ringing when I woke up
you woke up with it still ringing. that's one of those sounds that doesn't let go right away. what part of all that's stayed with you the most?
the black and white and the cake that never got smaller

the gray of it, and the knife sliding through the same soft white forever. those are the things your mind keeps. was there any thing in the dream that mattered to you, like an object you keep coming back to?

transcript.content:
hey

tell me a dream, however it comes back to you
it was like an old black and white film, grainy and flickering

grainy and flickering... like something half-faded, right at the edges of being remembered

what part of it felt most like that to you?
the stairs, i think. running up them and the same number on every wall, level 4, level 4, level 4

level 4 on every wall... that'd get under your skin after a while

were they going past you, the stairs? or behind you?
behind me, mostly. i kept running up and they just kept going, floor after floor. same number every time

like nothing was going to answer back, no matter how far you went up

and what were you running to? or from?
someone was following me, but every time i turned round there was only a thin grey dog sitting on the ramp watching me

a thin grey dog that just watches... not chasing, just there

did it feel like it was keeping pace with you somehow?
yeah, like no matter where i looked it was already there. waiting

so it wasn't just watching... it was ahead of you somehow, in the watching

were you scared of it? or was it something else?
not really scared. more uneasy. like it knew something i didn't

that's a lonely feeling, being watched by something that knows more than you do

when you saw it sitting there, did it ever look away, or was it just fixed on you?
it just sat and watched, didn't look away once

that kind of attention stays with you after waking, doesn't it

and how did it end?
i finally came out on the roof and it was raining, but the rain was falling upwards

falling upwards... that would make the roof feel upside down, like you'd run all that way just to reach somewhere backwards

what did that feel like, standing under it?
like the whole place was draining into the sky. i just stood there a second, not sure if i was really out

a second where even the inside of your own head feels like it's emptying out

were you still running in your mind, even standing still?
yeah, my legs still felt like they were moving. then i saw my car was there but it was a little wooden rowing boat parked between the lines

a rowing boat in the parking lines... like the roof had already decided it wasn't a roof anymore

did you get in, or just watch it?
i got in. the grey dog was already sitting in it

oh, already there... of course it was

was it still watching you the same way, now you were that close to it?
yeah, but it didn't seem threatening. more like it had been waiting for me to get in

like it had the whole thing timed, and you'd just done exactly what it expected

did the boat move once you were in it?
the roof filled with water around us and we floated. that's where i woke up

just floating, after all those stairs... it's almost gentle, the way it ends

did you wake up feeling like you'd come back through the water, or was it sudden?
sudden. like being pulled out of it all at once

pulled out before it had properly let you go

what stayed with you most, straight after?

so you slipped from watching into helping, almost without meaning to. and the corner was the moment.
yeah, exactly. one minute i'm a passenger, next i'm basically miming the controls when the corner comes. it felt natural though, not weird.

like your body just knew the moves.

was it just you and the conductor, or were there other people on the streetcar?
i don't remember anyone else on the streetcar. just me and the conductor, and all the machinery.

just the two of you, and all that brass and wood and the noise of it.

how did you feel, going through that corner with him?
alive, i guess. like we were doing something tricky and getting it right together. it felt good. not scary at all.

that's a lovely feeling. getting it right together, on the edge of the turn.

could you see the seat, the controls, the window?
i could see the lever clearly, and the conductor turning it. the rest is blurry, like a hand pushing a lever with nothing much around it. i don't remember a window or seats.

so the lever was the only solid thing. everything else just fell away.

was there any particular colour or texture you noticed in that bit?
the lever was dark, like old iron. smooth from use. the conductor's hand looked older. that's all i can picture.

that worn iron, and a hand that's done it a long time.

did the conductor look at you at all?
not that i remember. he was focused on the track. if he noticed me doing the lever, he didn't show it.

so it was wordless. just the two of you moving together for that one turn.

did anything about it feel like a dream, looking back? or did it all feel pretty ordinary until you woke up?
it felt ordinary until the next part, when i was suddenly on top of a train. that's when it got scary. but the streetcar bit felt real, like i could've been there.

so the streetcar could have actually happened, and then it tips into something else entirely.

was there a moment when you noticed the streetcar part ending? or was it just suddenly the train roof?]
suddenly the train roof. i don't remember leaving the streetcar or getting up there. one second lever, next second i'm high up and moving fast.
and now you're not sitting beside him at the controls. you're outside, on top, in the open air.
yeah, and it was much higher than a streetcar. like a proper train. the fear hit pretty fast because it was moving so fast and i kept nearly sliding off.

that's a brutal shift. one moment that good, wordless teamwork — then wind and speed and nothing to hold onto.

when you say you kept nearly sliding off, was there anything you could grab? or was it all just smooth metal?
just smooth metal, nothing to hold onto. i had to keep adjusting my balance. every time we went round a bend i thought i'd go over.

so the corner that felt so good on the streetcar is now the thing that might throw you off.

was there anyone else on the train roof with you? or on the train at all?
another family was sitting up there with me. a small baby was with them, and it seemed thrilled with the ride. i was the only one scared.
a baby, just delighted, right in the middle of what's terrifying you.
yeah, it made me feel worse, honestly. like they were all fine up there and i was the only one clinging and panicking. the baby was having the time of its life.

so it wasn't just that you were scared. it was feeling like the odd one out in a place where everyone else seemed to belong.

what was the baby doing that made it seem so happy up there?
laughing, i think. i remember the baby looking around wide-eyed and just looking happy. not worried at all. i don't remember who was holding it or if it was sitting.
wide-eyed and laughing at all that speed and wind. as if the whole thing was made for it.
yeah. i felt like there was something wrong with me for being scared. i even thought i might try to jump off, especially on the bends. i didn't, but the thought scared me more.

that's a heavy thought to carry on the roof of a moving train. especially after the streetcar, where you were so sure of your hands and feet.

was the sky or the land anything? or was it all just speed and metal?
the train was on a country road, so i knew we were passing fields or something. but i was mostly watching the roof and the edge. i don't remember the sky.

so all your attention was on ordinary not falling. no time to really see what you were passing.

were they sitting together?
the family seemed more at ease, like they were out for a nice ride. i didn't get whether they were sitting close or spread out. the baby was just somewhere among them.

so you were on a streetcar, watching the conductor at first. then as you went round a sharp corner, you felt like you were driving it with him, going through the motions of the lever. it felt natural and alive, getting it right together. the lever was old dark iron, smooth from use, and his hand looked older. just the two of you and the machinery, wordless. then suddenly you were on top of a train, high up and moving fast on a country road, with smooth metal and nothing to hold onto, and you kept nearly sliding off on bends. another family was up there, at ease, with a small baby laughing and thrilled, but you were the only one scared, and you even thought of jumping off but didn't.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. that's how it was. i can't think of anything you missed.

thanks. i have enough.

that's interesting—your body just knew what to do, even when nothing under you felt solid.

was that easiness part of what felt dreamlike, or did it feel natural to you while it was happening?
It felt natural while it was happening, like that's just how that world worked. I didn't question it.

of course. dreams are like that—you don't stop to ask why the world works the way it does.

and all this time, you were in your own body? or did it feel like you were somewhere above it all, just watching?
I was in my own body, walking through it. It didn't feel like watching from outside or floating—I was inside it all, moving around.

inside it the whole way through.

and you said the waiting—did it end, or did you just wake up?
I think I just woke up. I don't remember the waiting ending, or anything happening after that. It just stopped.

so it never really finished, just stopped when you did.

was there anything with you in that walked world—a particular object, or a thing that mattered more than the rest?
No, everything seemed about the same importance. Just blurry, glowing shapes in the glass haze. Nothing that drew me more than anything else.

so you were at your parents' house after a long trip, just waiting. you tried to step through the window, but everything on the other side was glass too—a blurry haze with trees, grass, and rocks all glowing from inside themselves, a pale cold light that felt cold to look at. it was silent, no one else around, and the glass wasn't a barrier—it was the whole place. you walked slow through it, the ground having no feel but moving easy, not knowing what you were waiting for, and then it just stopped when you woke up.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
You got it right. That's pretty much exactly how it felt.

that's good to hear. i can almost see it from here.

would you like me to help you turn it into a picture?
Yeah, I'd like that.

there are a few ways I could draw it. one is frosted glass etching, where the whole world looks like scratched frost on a pane, soft and monochrome. another is cold mist airbrush, everything painted in thin veils of cold air, hazy and insubstantial. a third is a luminous glass mosaic, like a window made of many small panes each glowing softly from within. or I could do a faithful sketch of the dream as you saw it, a blurry world of glowing shapes behind glass, cold and silent. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
The frosty one—that feels right. Like everything soft and cold and blurred on the glass.

ok, i'll start with you, then i'll draw you too, since you're in it.

how would you like to be drawn—as you are, if you want to tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
